narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Calmer than yesterday; temperatures and cloud little changed. Largely dry, with thunder possible, peaking this evening again. 31°C / 88°F high, 20°C / 68°F low. Sky partly cloudy early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NNE early and SW at midday; gusts to 37 km/h (20 kt). UV index 9.4 (very high). Air quality 88 (moderate), by the CAMS model. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C / 73°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 7 km/h; sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS see temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Saturday will be mostly cloudy with highs between 27°C and 32°C, and three of four models wet. Sunday remains mostly cloudy, highs 29–32°C, two of four models wet. Monday stays mostly cloudy, highs 30–32°C, two of four models wet, and the call predicts rain with a 65 % chance. RECORD shows the best rain record for Day+3 belongs to ICON.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunder today is supported by high CAPE values: Best Match 2410 J/kg, ECMWF 2650 J/kg, GFS 1420 J/kg, ICON 2390 J/kg, and UKMO 3230 J/kg, peaking at 18:00. This raises the risk of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No specific bulletin from the Kenya Meteorological Department warns of severe weather at this time.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind is northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 9 km/h (5 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt), and westerly into the evening at 14 km/h (7 kt) gusting 23 km/h (12 kt). Peak gust reaches 25 km/h (14 kt). Thunder possible this evening adds a gust hazard beyond the forecast.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1014 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest, southwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.6 and 1014.8 hPa, falling by 1.9 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -1.6 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, and Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind. ECMWF slightly under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind, while GFS slightly over-forecasts cloud cover and highs and under-forecasts peak wind. The call's high of 31°C (88°F) sits within the spread of the models, which range from 22°C to 31.2°C. ICON holds the best rain record for Day+3, but its Day+0 rain probability is low. KMD forecasts a max of 30°C, close to the call, and mentions light showers and thunderstorms likely. DATA SUFFICIENCY shows 53 checks at Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven coverage.
